reaudit_history: Mechanical re-stamp by `./le rfc reseal`. Every verdict re-stamped below was in the SHIFTED state: its recorded unit fingerprints -- the enclosing top-level function of each tagged test -- were byte-identical to the tree, and only the file around them had moved (a line shift, a sibling test, an import rewrite). Nothing about what any of these tests asserts changed, so no verdict was re-judged and only the `tests` map was rewritten. A verdict whose unit, cited producer code, or requirement text moved was REFUSED and left stale for a human. The proof is the code in verdict_freshness(), not this note.

RFC5282-3-1.note: Forbidden: a receiver refusing a message for its Padding length (0..255). Red: TestRFC5282AEADReceiveAcceptsAnyPaddingTo255 fatals 'decryptAndParse = %v, want the message accepted' for every length 0..255. Negative TestRFC5282AEADReceiveRefusesATruncatedInnerPayload bounds it (expectRefused).

RFC5282-3.1-1.note: Forbidden: an IV other than eight octets. Sender: TestRFC5282AEADSendIVIsEightOctets opens ze's LastSentMsg with the first 8 octets as IV and asserts gotIVOctets == 8. Receiver: TestRFC5282AEADReceiveRefusesAnIVThatIsNotEightOctets expectRefused for 7 and 9. The IV length is the shared ikeIVOctets for GCM and CCM.

RFC5282-3.1-2.note: Forbidden: an IV repeated under one key. Red: TestRFC5282AEADSendIVIsUniquePerKey fatals on any repeat over 512 builds under one SA; TestRFC5282AEADSendIVDoesNotRepeatForARepeatedMessage fatals when two byte-identical builds share an IV.

RFC5282-3.2-1.note: Forbidden: not supporting the 16 octet AES GCM ICV. Red: TestRFC5282AEADSendICVIsSixteenOctets asserts len(raw)==prefix+IV+plaintext+16 and expectOneDelete on the receiver; TestRFC5282AEADReceiveRefusesADamagedICV proves the 16 octets are verified (flipped and stripped ICV refused).

RFC5282-3.2-2.note: Forbidden: supporting an AES GCM ICV other than 16, 8, 12. Red: TestRFC5282AEADRefusesAForbiddenICVLength fatals if OpenIKEAEAD(ENCR_AES_GCM_16) accepts a real 13, 14 or 15 octet ICV sealing; TestRFC5282AEADOpensTheFullLengthICV keeps 16 open. Lengths below 12 are not constructed (stdlib limit); ze's only GCM transform (20) fixes the tag at 16, so no other length is reachable.

RFC5282-3.2-3.note: Forbidden: not supporting AES CCM ICVs of 8 and 16. Red: TestRFC5282CCMSupportsTheEightAndSixteenOctetICV establishes under CCM8 and CCM16, measures the ICV (t.Errorf on mismatch) and expectOneDelete; TestRFC5282CCMVerifiesTheEightAndSixteenOctetICV refuses a flipped ICV bit and a flipped ciphertext bit at each size.

RFC5282-3.2-4.note: Forbidden: an AES CCM ICV length other than 8, 16, 12. Red: TestRFC5282CCMRefusesEveryOtherICVLength sweeps Transform IDs 0..35, errors if AEADICVOctets answers a length outside {8,12,16} or answers for any id beyond 14,15,16,20, and requires SealIKEAEAD/OpenIKEAEAD to refuse the rest; TestRFC5282CCMSupportsTheThreePermittedICVLengths seals and opens 8, 12 and 16.

RFC5282-4-1.note: Encryptor: TestRFC5282AEADSendSealsUnderSaltThenIV opens the real initiator IKE_AUTH request and responder response with an independent stdlib AES-GCM under salt||IV and refuses IV||salt (same length, order alone); SealIKEAEAD (crypto/aead.go) is the only seal site. Decryptor: TestRFC5282AEADNonceIsSaltThenIV accepts salt||IV, TestRFC5282AEADRefusesAReversedNonce refuses the reversed nonce. The ikeAEADNonce record is a whole-producer panic (reach); discrimination read from the independent-oracle assertions.

RFC5282-4-2.note: Forbidden: an AES GCM nonce other than 12 octets. Red: TestRFC5282AEADNonceIsTwelveOctets asserts len(nonce)==12 and expectOneDelete; TestRFC5282AEADRefusesANonceThatIsNotTwelveOctets refuses 11 and 13. Sender side: the nonce size is fixed once in newIKEAEAD (salt+ikeIVOctets, checked by newAESGCM) and shared by SealIKEAEAD and OpenIKEAEAD, and Go's AEAD panics on a wrong-length nonce, so a sender-only length change is not reachable without reddening the receive units.

RFC5282-4-3.note: Forbidden: an AES CCM nonce not built as salt||IV. Encryptor: TestRFC5282CCMNonceIsSaltThenIV opens ze's own sent message with an independent CCM under the 3 salt octets then the wire IV (fatal on failure). Decryptor: TestRFC5282CCMRefusesAReversedNonce refuses IV||salt.

RFC5282-4-4.note: Forbidden: an AES CCM nonce other than 11 octets. Red: TestRFC5282CCMNonceIsElevenOctets asserts len(nonce)==11 and expectOneDelete; TestRFC5282CCMRefusesANonceThatIsNotElevenOctets refuses 10 and 12. Sender length is fixed by the shared newIKEAEAD (ccm.New with salt+IV), so a sender-only change is not reachable without reddening these.

RFC5282-5.1-1.note: Sender: TestRFC5282AEADSendAssociatedDataRunsThroughTheSKHeader pins DataOffset 32 on both ends' real messages and opens them under raw[:32] with an independent AES-GCM, not under raw[:31] nor the fixed header alone; auth.go buildSKMessageAEADWithMsgID is the only seal site. Receiver: TestRFC5282AEADAssociatedDataCoversAnInterveningPayload accepts the span over an intervening payload, TestRFC5282AEADRefusesAnAlteredInterveningPayload refuses an altered one.

RFC5282-5.1-2.note: Sender: TestRFC5282AEADSendAssociatedDataExcludesTheIVAndCiphertext opens both ends' real messages under the span stopping before the IV and refuses AAD covering the IV and IV+ciphertext. Receiver: TestRFC5282AEADAssociatedDataExcludesTheIVAndCiphertext accepts, TestRFC5282AEADRefusesAssociatedDataCoveringTheIV refuses.

RFC5282-7.1-1.note: Both ciphers the clause names are now proven. AES GCM: TestRFC5282AEADIntegrityKeysAreZeroOctets (zero-length SK_ai/SK_ar, SK_ei at the prf+ offset right after SK_d). AES CCM: new TestRFC5282CCMIntegrityKeysAreZeroOctets derives every CCM Transform ID (8/12/16) at 128 and 256 bits and asserts SK_ai/SK_ar zero octets AND SK_ei/SK_er at stream offsets 32 and 32+(n+3) computed independently of the producer, so a derivation that returned empty slices while still consuming integrity material turns red. Negative: TestRFC5282NonAEADIntegrityKeysAreDerived (non-AEAD keeps its integrity keys). Records: DeriveSKKeys revert observed red on all three units (panic reverts; the offset assertions are what discriminate a mis-cut stream).

RFC5282-7.1-2.note: Both bullets proven. AES GCM bullet: TestRFC5282AEADEncryptionKeysCarryTheirSalt (20/36 octets, key-then-salt round trip). AES CCM bullet: new TestRFC5282CCMEncryptionKeysCarryTheirSalt, every CCM ID at 128/256 bits: SK_ei and SK_er are exactly cipher key + 3 octets (19/35), and a SealIKEAEAD output is opened by a ccm instance built in the test from key[:n] with nonce = trailing 3 salt octets || 8-octet IV, which is the RFC 4309 Section 7.1 KEYMAT format and Section 4 nonce; a 4-octet GCM salt or salt-first layout fails the length or the open. Negative: TestRFC5282NonAEADEncryptionKeysCarryNoSalt. Records: SealIKEAEAD and encKeyMaterialLen reverts observed red. Residual: the opener uses ze's own internal/core/ccm package, so it checks the key split, not the CCM primitive itself.

RFC5282-7.3-1.note: AES GCM: TestRFC5282AEADProposalCarriesTheKeyLengthAttribute (IKE and ESP rails, exactly one attribute), TestRFC5282AEADOfferWithoutAKeyLengthIsRefused (ErrKeyLengthMissing). AES CCM: TestRFC5282AEADCCMProposalCarriesTheKeyLengthAttribute asserts IDs 14/15/16 x 128/256 each carry exactly one Key Length attribute of the key size from buildWireIKEProposals; ESP does not offer CCM (ipsec.EncryptionImplementedESP excludes it). Residual observation: the receive-side refusal names CCM in keyLengthRequired but only a GCM offer is driven.

RFC5282-8-1.note: IKE SA: TestRFC5282AEADSelectionCarriesNoIntegrityAlgorithm / TestRFC5282AEADOfferWithIntegrityIsRefused. ESP SA, initiator re-check: TestRFC5282AEADESPSelectionCarriesNoIntegrityAlgorithm / TestRFC5282AEADESPOfferWithIntegrityIsRefused. ESP SA, responder (where Ze selects the Child SA's algorithms): TestRFC5282ResponderSelectsNoIntegrityForAnAEADChildSA runs selectResponderESP over an AES-GCM-only SAi2 with Hash configured, then espProposalToWire over the selection exactly as buildAuthResponse does, and asserts one AES GCM transform and zero INTEG transforms in SAr2; TestRFC5282ResponderRefusesAnAEADChildSAOfferWithIntegrity refuses AES-GCM + HMAC-SHA2-256 with ErrNoProposalChosen and accepts no proposal. Records revert responder.go::espProposalMatches. Re-judged 2026-09-30 after espProposalMatches gained the Section 3.3.6 emptied-type refusal: the AEAD+INTEG refusal path is untouched (the INTEG transform in the negative carries no unknown attribute), both records re-recorded and observed red, all six units pass.

RFC5282-8-2.note: IKE proposal: TestRFC5282AEADIKEProposalCarriesNoIntegrityTransform / TestRFC5282NonAEADIKEProposalKeepsItsIntegrityTransform. ESP proposal: TestRFC5282AEADESPProposalCarriesNoIntegrityTransform (AES-GCM with Hash configured: zero Transform Type 3, ENCR and ESN kept) and TestRFC5282NonAEADESPProposalKeepsItsIntegrityTransform (AES-CBC: exactly one). espProposalToWire is the single ESP builder (IKE_AUTH offer, CREATE_CHILD_SA offer and answer).
